# Risk & Resilience portfolio (6 projects)

Built to evidence the essential criteria of a Risk & Resilience Specialist role in a digital-led retailer:
risk registers and KRIs, business impact analysis and continuity, scenario testing, incident learning,
stakeholder-ready insight, and using data to find themes and changes in exposure.

**All data is synthetic** (generated by the scripts with fixed seeds) and every company, system and figure is fictional
or an explicit assumption. Nothing here uses real company data. Each project says what its synthetic data can and
cannot prove.

| # | Project | Shows | Role criteria it supports |
|---|---------|-------|---------------------------|
| 1 | [Predictive KRI early-warning](p1_kri_early_warning/README.md) | Forecast a KRI 2 weeks ahead, alert before tolerance is breached | KRIs, analytics, leadership dashboards |
| 2 | [NLP on incidents and audit actions](p2_incident_nlp/README.md) | Turn free text into themes, trends and overdue-action hotspots | Themes, action follow-through, root causes |
| 3 | [Dependency network analysis](p3_dependency_network/README.md) | Single points of failure, third-party concentration, RTO conflicts | BIA, dependency mapping, third parties |
| 4 | [Monte Carlo disruption simulation](p4_disruption_montecarlo/README.md) | Loss distribution vs impact tolerance, value of the continuity plan | Scenario testing, resilience, commercial judgement |
| 5 | [AI risk and resilience assessment](p5_ai_risk_assessment/README.md) | Drift monitoring, fallback design and an AI risk register | Technology risk, change, emerging risk |
| 6 | [BIA and continuity plan](p6_bia_continuity_plan/README.md) | Impact over time, RTOs, workarounds, roles and testing for a critical process (document) | BIA, continuity planning, incident response |

## Run it
```
pip install -r requirements.txt
./run_all.sh        # or: cd p1_kri_early_warning && python3 kri_early_warning.py
```

## How to use this for applications
- Put each project on your portfolio site as a one-page case study: problem, approach, finding, recommended action, limitations.
- In interviews lead with the finding and the decision it supports, not the model. Each README ends with a
  "what I would tell leadership" paragraph to practise from.
- Be upfront that the data is synthetic and say how you would validate with real data. That honesty is a strength in a risk role.
